prerequisites: Ability to calculate internal forces or section forces for statically determinate and indeterminate prismatic elements.
Knowledge of basic concepts of continuum mechanics, especially stress and strain.
Ability to determine stresses and deformations for the cross-section for each type of section force (normal force, shear force, and bending moment).
Knowledge of basic concepts of the limit state method.

learning_outcomes.text: The student is able to design a reinforced concrete section of prismatic elements based on stresses and deformations across the cross-section, according to the limit state method.

The studied load cases include: simple compression (excluding column buckling), simple bending (rectangular and T-sections), and shear force, including the connection of secondary and primary beams (node).
The student acquires insight into execution requirements and practical detailing such as necessary concrete cover, min/max reinforcement section, and minimum concrete dimensions.
At the end of the course, students should be able to calculate prismatic non-slender columns and beams.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to the limit state method, specifically for concrete and reinforcing steel.
Dimensioning of non-slender prismatic columns subjected to centric compression.
Dimensioning of prismatic beams subjected to simple bending moment and shear force.
Execution requirements and practical detailing (necessary concrete cover, min/max reinforcement section, minimum concrete dimensions).
Design of prismatic structural elements according to the limit state method through practical examples.
Studied load cases in practical examples: simple compression (excluding buckling) for columns, simple bending for beams, shear force for beams.

Application of execution requirements and practical detailing such as: position of reinforcing bars in the section and along the length of the prismatic element, minimum dimensions of the concrete section.

assessment_methods.method: Written exam during the examination period
